reviews.title: Appreciate the Features, Concerned About the Content
reviews.body:
I really appreciate the features of the Dwell app, especially the ability to make playlists, use CarPlay, and listen to Scripture throughout my day. These tools help me stay rooted in God's Word.

That said, I have some concerns about certain parts of the app. As a Bible-believing Christian, I want to stay away from practices that resemble New Age or mystical spirituality. Some of the content, like breath prayers and Lectio Divina, feels more emotional or contemplative than scriptural. I’ve noticed a few reflections that shift the focus away from God’s Word and instead direct people toward experiences or inner impressions.

I still use the app, but I intentionally avoid those sections. I would love to see a version of Dwell that focuses solely on Scripture readings, with no added prayer prompts or meditative practices. That kind of content would give users like me full confidence in what we’re hearing and sharing with others.

Thank you for creating a platform that makes listening to the Bible more accessible. I pray that the content continues to grow in a direction that keeps God's Word at the center.

I though these sorts of dark patterns in user experience design were a thing of the past in ‘modern’ apps. This might even violate Apple’s user experience guidelines, which I believe state that an app ought to have some sort of basic experience upon first run before payment is required. I should not have to enter my card details to get a taste of the app. Why not include one book to listen to? If you’re going to give a 7 day trial, why require my card details and ‘auto-renew’ first? I’ve been put off the app by this aggressive and disappointing sales tactic.

I thought I’d give this one a week to see how I like it. It doesn’t show up in my settings as a subscription (ios), which means I can’t cancel until I decide. I regularly do this with a new app that has a trial so I can test it out, without ‘accidentally’ getting charged full price if I don’t want the app. 
Can’t find that. So disappointing when companies make it difficult to manage. If it sells through the App Store, it should be available in my subscriptions. 
So how do I cancel?? Apparently I have to go to the website. Probably go thru a big song and dance just to FIND my account (as in sign up, verify email etc etc etc). I guess they’re hoping you’ll give up and just pay. Not nice!

Neat concept with tools many of us have been waiting for, but still a lot missing and poor execution. Pretty ugly UI that doesn't manage all the options well. No option to cast to a smart speaker. Some audio is engaging but most seems to be monotone. Most everything is behind the paywall, so you'll only be blessed by this app if you have a lot of extra $$$$$

reviews.title: Dishonest
reviews.body: You need to let people know that they need to pay a subscription fee to use it. Yes, you get a free trial but you really shouldn’t waist people’s time by making it free to download but then making it a subscription. I didn’t see you state that anywhere in the description.

It's really unfortunate this company feels the need to lock the gospel up behind a pay wall. I know it's $30 a year but it seems a little outlandish considering there's other apps that do this same thing but for free.

From the reviews, I thought, "great, an app that will read the Word to me". Why does it need access to anything, and why do I need to sign up?

The ad is very misleading. The content before subscription is great, but it is a steep price to pay. If it was a one-off fee, it might be more enticing for people. The content I can get is great but wish we had access to more as it has helped hugely with my Quiet Time.

reviews.body: The app is brilliant. But I don’t understand the functions. When listening to the yearly plan and I tick that I have read it, it doesn’t keep the information. I also miss that once I have red a section that I will be taken automatically to the next passage instead of having to find the plan anew each time. What do I do wrong?

reviews.body: I liked the first voice then they put in this other woman who reads too slowly and too over dramatically.

reviews.title: Room for improvement
reviews.body: Backed this on Kickstarter as was super keen to have a Bible app I could listen to, but it sounds like individual verses have been recorded separately and the intonation of the voices is therefore very bizarre in places. Also, the voices chosen are actually quite strange. There doesn’t appear to be any voices with people just reading the Bible like a person would. There’s too much drama. A project like this ultimately rises and falls based upon available voices, but currently none of them really cut it. A bit sad really as I’ve subscribed for a year.
